subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The current source path and user impact are clear, but the requested fix changes sandbox write semantics that affect security expectations and currently documented/read-tested behavior.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox-local writes, and require a complete mount, bridge, tool, docs, and regression-test update.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Confirm the current security model, update docs/support guidance around writable sandbox workflows, and close or reframe the report accordingly.

options.title: Fold into broader bind policy
options.body: Defer this exact semantic change until the least-privilege writable-bind design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox-local writes, and require a complete mount, bridge, tool, docs, and regression-test update.

likelyOwner.reason: The sandbox history points to Peter Steinberger for the owner-boundary decision, and the likely fix would touch security-owned sandbox code.
